Use case: identity-preserve. Production game animation sprites, FOUR COMPLETE WHOLE FIGURES, one physically coherent robot plus held hammer drawn together in each image. Transparent 2x2 sheet, four equally spaced square cells, maximum detail/resolution, no labels or grid.
Reference1 is Chronos, preserve this exact finned black helmet/cyan visor, chest blue disc, black/chrome armor, proportions, boots and metallic pixel-art look. Reference2 is the exact blue T-SHAPED mallet: blue electric cylinder with black caps/blue end circles, black segmented shaft connected to its SIDE CENTER. Do not redesign it.
These are four close sequential poses at the BOTTOM of an overhead hammer strike. Constant frontal camera, boots planted wide at the same baseline, slight deep squat, torso leaning into the blow.
TOP LEFT: arms driving down, hammer shaft at a shallow diagonal ACROSS the waist, head to the character's RIGHT (viewer right).
TOP RIGHT: impact. The entire handle is HORIZONTAL across his waist and held by BOTH FISTS SIDE BY SIDE ON THE HANDLE. BOTTOM RIGHT: recovery rebound, the whole two-handed horizontal hammer grip lifting slightly back toward waist/chest, keeping the exact same side-center head connection.
The right-side hammer head and its LOWER END CAP must be clearly visible in EVERY pose. Hands are left of the head, the shaft passes through both fists. Character/arms/weapon are drawn as one complete integrated pose, not a prop pasted onto empty-handed art. All four poses same robot, head, weapon size, body unit, materials, and camera. Full head-to-boots bodies and whole hammer fit each cell with padding.
Style: sharp authored HD 16-bit Neo-Geo pixel clusters, clean dark outlines and controlled metallic highlights, matching references, not painted/blurry. Transparent empty background, no cast shadows, no glow clouds, no motion lines, no impact effects or lettering.
